description: We're a team passionate about space, engineering, and technology! Our skills include Fusion 360, basic electronics, photography, drone technology, and experience contributing to an asteroid research paper. This is our first hackathon, and we're here to learn, have fun, and build something cool! We're looking for teammates skilled in coding, 3D modeling, or hardware development.
summary:
Inspired by the Mongolian Empire’s historic Өртөө (Urtuu) relay network, **Team Astor introduces URTUU**, an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform designed to support safer, more connected planetary exploration.

Future Mars missions face significant challenges, including hazardous terrain, limited communications, environmental risks, and the absence of operational global GPS infrastructure.

**URTUU addresses these challenges** by integrating interactive planetary maps, rover route planning, 3D terrain visualization, mission simulation, and a conceptual network of autonomous Өртөө stations.

Our primary mission focuses on **Arsia Mons**, a Martian volcano where NASA Mars Odyssey observations have revealed candidate cave skylights. These sites offer promising opportunities for geological research, astrobiology, and future underground habitats.

Our working prototype includes Mars mapping, navigation tools, station network functionality, terrain visualization, and simulated exploration missions.

URTUU also connects Mars exploration with Mongolia’s **Gobi Desert**, proposing Khermen Tsav and Tsagaan Suvarga as analog testing regions for robotic navigation and geological research.

By combining **NASA planetary science, modern geospatial technology, and Mongolian historical innovation**, URTUU presents a scalable vision for future autonomous exploration infrastructure on Mars.
details:
The Problem

NASA missions have produced extensive scientific observations of Mars, but human explorers need practical tools that bring geographical information, terrain analysis, navigation, and mission operations together.

Astronauts must be able to investigate scientifically valuable locations while considering terrain obstacles, travel distance, available energy, communication limitations, and environmental uncertainties.

Mars also lacks the global navigation infrastructure people rely on Earth.

URTUU addresses this challenge by exploring how mission-planning software and distributed surface infrastructure could work together.

Our Exploration Mission

Our primary scenario is a simulated crewed expedition around Arsia Mons.

We focus on three named candidate cave skylights:

  • Annie
  • Dena
  • Chloë

Our mission concept involves travelling between these scientific sites, investigating potentially accessible underground environments, and assessing their relevance to future human exploration.

The software supports route design and navigation planning for the scenario.

The proposed regional expedition is a planning exercise, not a validated or NASA-approved traverse. Actual travel feasibility would require higher-resolution terrain analysis, rover engineering constraints, and additional safety assessments.

What We Built

1. Interactive Martian Map

Our prototype includes an interactive map for exploring the Martian surface and planning mission locations.

It provides the geographic foundation for our rover navigation and scientific exploration scenarios.

2. Rover Route Planning

We implemented route-planning functionality that allows exploration paths to be designed and visualized.

This helps users investigate the geographic relationships between mission locations and consider alternative traverse plans.

Route results are planning outputs, not guarantees of safe rover passage.

3. 3D Terrain Visualization

We implemented a 3D terrain view to help users understand the landscape and visualize proposed exploration routes.

This supports a more intuitive understanding of the terrain than a conventional flat map alone.

4. Өртөө Station Network

Our core innovation is a simulated distributed network inspired by the historical Mongolian Өртөө system.

The concept includes four station types:

  • URT-H: Mission coordination hubs.
  • URT-S: Environmental sensing and navigation-reference stations.
  • URT-R: Communication relay stations.
  • URT-C: Energy support depots.

Our prototype includes Өртөө network functionality for exploration planning.

The concept is intended to complement onboard rover navigation rather than independently replace GPS.

5. Mission Simulation

We implemented mission simulation functionality so users can explore rover operations and hypothetical mission scenarios.

Simulation helps communicate how route choices, infrastructure, and changing conditions could influence exploration decisions.

Simulated environmental readings and vehicle behavior must not be confused with actual Mars observations.

6. Mongolian Gobi Analog Mapping

Our software includes Gobi mapping functionality connected to our proposed Earth analog mission.

We selected two scientifically interesting regions:

Khermen Tsav, Ömnögovi Province: A proposed environment for studying robotic terrain navigation, reconnaissance, and distributed station deployment.

Tsagaan Suvarga, Dundgovi Province: A proposed environment for geological field exercises, route planning, and terrain hazard observation.

These locations are proposed future testing environments. Our team has not claimed to have constructed physical stations or completed astronaut field training there.

Scientific Objectives

Our Arsia Mons scenario focuses on:

  • Investigating potential lava tube and cave skylight environments.
  • Understanding terrain accessibility around scientific targets.
  • Considering environmental risks during human exploration.
  • Studying possible applications of subsurface environments for future habitats.
  • Exploring how distributed monitoring and navigation infrastructure could assist future missions.

Potential Martian caves remain scientifically uncertain, and the named skylights should not be treated as confirmed accessible underground habitats.

Technology and System Design

URTUU is a browser-based geospatial mission-control application.

Its implemented software capabilities include:

  • Interactive geographic mapping.
  • 3D terrain visualization.
  • Route planning and visualization.
  • Network-based station simulation.
  • Mission scenario simulation.
  • Earth analog geographic mapping.

Our development design uses a modern web-application architecture with separate geographic, routing, network, and simulation functionality.

The project has been designed for eventual public deployment through Vercel.

Our proposed architecture also provides a path toward future integration of additional NASA data layers, physical environmental sensors, drone imagery, and more advanced navigation algorithms.

Innovation

URTUU's main innovation is combining three ideas:

Mongolian heritage: Reimagining the historical Өртөө relay network as distributed planetary exploration infrastructure.

Integrated mission planning: Connecting maps, routes, terrain visualization, surface stations, and simulated operations in one application.

Earth-to-Mars development: Connecting a Martian scientific mission with potential field testing in the Mongolian Gobi.

We envision a future in which locally deployed surface stations could contribute information to a larger exploration network, helping robotic and human explorers make better-informed decisions.

Future Development

Our next steps include improving terrain-risk models, validating numerical scientific layers, testing positioning algorithms, integrating drone reconnaissance data, and investigating real sensor-station prototypes.

Longer-term development could include authorized field experiments in the Gobi Desert and structured analog mission exercises.
